lines.text: What if gold was as common as iron?
Today, all the gold ever mined would fit in a cube about twenty two metres wide.
Day one. Gold turns up in every hill and backyard.
Its price collapses, and wedding rings are suddenly worth about as much as nails.
Week one. Families who saved in gold lose those savings overnight.
Central banks, holding around thirty nine thousand tonnes, watch it become ordinary metal.

segments.caption: Gold gets useful
segments.fact: NEVER RUSTS · ONLY SILVER & COPPER CONDUCT BETTER

lines.text: Month three. Then people notice what gold is good at.
It never rusts, and only silver and copper carry electricity better.
Year one. Wiring, pipes and gutters are made of gold, and none of it corrodes.
But gold is soft, and about two and a half times heavier than iron.
A gold bike bends, and a gold car would be painfully heavy, so steel still does the heavy lifting.
Year ten. Golden roofs bounce back the sun's heat, the same trick astronauts' visors use.
Gold stops being treasure, and becomes one of the most useful metals we have.
So, would you still want a gold ring?
